working_definition: Lawf2 (lamina wide-field neuron 2) is an optic-lobe interneuron with wide-field arborisations spanning multiple lamina cartridges, distinct from its sister type Lawf1 and from the columnar lamina monopolar and centrifugal neurons. It was identified directly at res-2.0 using eya, hth and Lim1 co-expression, with Lim1 the additional marker distinguishing it from Lawf1 (Chen et al., 2016).

best_match.fbbt_definition: A lamina wide-field neuron that has a main projection into the lamina making wide-field arborizations in the distal lamina, innervating 28 cartridges. These neurons also arborize in the medulla (Hasegawa et al., 2011). In the M1 layer, the branches are large and overlapping, encompassing around 120 cartridges. In medulla layers M8 to M10 the branches are smaller, encompassing around 17 cartridges and show less overlap. Putative cholinergic presynaptic sites are observed in the lamina.

justification: FBbt:00110065 is the sister lamina wide-field type to Lawf1, matching the report's Lawf2 (wide-field arborisation spanning multiple cartridges, distinguished from Lawf1 by additional Lim1 expression). Label provenance is clean (GEO = Table S2, no REVIEW flag, no subclustering performed), and this is an adult brain atlas for which the mature adult form is appropriate.
recommendation: Accept as exact match at high confidence.
